newsitem.title: USA: Colombia sells variety of spot crudes for January.
newsitem.headline: Colombia sells variety of spot crudes for January.

text.p: Colombia's state owned oil company Ecopetrol sold a variety of spot crude cargoes into the U.S. Gulf Coast and Latin America, amid other regional spot activity, trade sources said Tuesday.

The company sold at least one cargo of Vasconia for mid-January to a Gulf Coast refiner. The refiner is reoffering the crude at February West Texas Intermediate minus $1.85 a barrel fob, the sources said.
Ecopetrol also sold Cano Limon and South Blend cargoes to Spain's Repsol for the La Pampilla refinery in Peru, the sources added.
The Cano Limon was sold at around Feb WTI minus $1.35-45 a barrel, while the South Blend went for around Feb WTI minus $2.15 a barrel. Both cargoes are for end-January, traders said.
Finally, Ecopetrol was heard to have sold a cargo of Cusiana to state owned Petroleos de Venezuela unit Maraven at around Feb WTI plus 45 cents, traders said.
"The Venezuelans are probably trying to free up their Furrial crude for export," one trader noted.
Separately, British Petroleum sold a Cusiana cargo for loading December 30-31 into the Gulf Coast at Feb WTI plus 47 cents.
Meanwhile, Shell sold Vasconia for January 5-9 to a Gulf Coast refiner in a confidential trasncation.
Elsewhere, Chile's state owned oil company Empresa Nacional del Petroleo (ENAP) issued a tender for 960,000 barrels for delivery January 28 to February 2.
